I've been interested for years about diving. I'm currently living in Michigan, but I plan to move more towards the west coast within the next few years. I was wondering if anyone knows of the best ways to get started with diving?
How would you recommend one get started?

We recently did it on vacation. You can get certified within a few days. There are dive clubs back in the states you can join as well, just search in your area. They dive lakes and pools.

What I absolutely love about diving is that it's a culture that's big on safety. So every step of the way, you practice good habits and procedures before something goes wrong.

Pretty much this. Anywhere you go in the states should have a dive center not too too far. Even Nashville (where I'm from) has a number and it's completely landlocked. Find a place that does PADI Open Water certification (that's the most common dive organization I believe and I'd argue the most accepted around the world as far as standards go). They should provide you with everything you need during the course including fins, wetsuit, BCD, etc etc.

Yep, as @rocketbrainsurgeon and @mr_mellow3 said - look up your local (or local to where you'll be moving) dive shop, which are usually referred to as LDS - and ask about their prices and what agency they do their certifications through (PADI, SSI, etc).

You'll likely want to visit the shop and have a look at what they offer by way of education, gear and trips. You'll also want to speak to the instructors and employees, make sure that you're comfortable with them and you don't get any bad vibes. One big rule I always tell friends to follow is to make sure you are 100% comfortable with your instructor! If you get a bad vibe, they have a nasty attitude or just plain out don't teach well - WALK AWAY! This is your safety and in all reality, your life on the line - you don't want to be taught by someone who is rude, moves too quickly, makes you feel inept or dumb, etc.

Check out reviews for the shop on Yelp and perhaps even in diving communities that have regional sections (the scubaboard.com forums are one example).

That's most of what I can think of off of the top of my head, but feel free to ask any questions regarding specifics and I'll do my best to help! I've got quite a few close friends that are instructors and a couple course directors as well, so if I don't know an answer to a question - I can find out!

Good luck and HAVE FUN! That's what this is all about. :)
